description:
Philip talks about how to invest wisely with your assets and how to make your money grow I'm a professional problem solver. I help entrepreneurs, investors, corporate officers, innovators, shareholders, and financiers alike—ranging from established Fortune 100 corporations with worldwide reach, all the way to nonprofit organizations in the middle of west Texas—creatively solve their problems and secure the future of their endeavors through bespoke legal and business solutions to overcome their unique challenges. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why you’re bad at fundraising—and how to fix it | Philip Wiseman | TEDxMidland

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"It’s not the splash you remember, it’s the dive." ⚽️?

In this inspiring and funny talk, England legend Jill Scott takes us on a journey from being the only girl on an all boys team in Sunderland to winning the Euros at Wembley. Jill shares the raw reality of her 161-cap career, reflecting on the resilience required to thrive in a sport that, for a long time, didn't even have a professional path for women. Whether you're a football fan or looking for leadership insights, Jill’s story is a masterclass in staying true to yourself while working toward a collective goal.

Jill discusses..
·         Building resilience from a young age.
·         Why comparing yourself to others is a trap.
·         How knowing what motivates your teammates (from new kitchens to family) changes how you play for them.
·         How Sarina Wiegman’s "black and white" approach led the Lionesses to European glory.
·         Why the memories and friendships (the "dive") matter more than the final result (the "
title: The real secret behind winning the Euros (it's not what you think) | Jill Scott | TEDxManchester

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Kylie Moffitt redefines what it means to heal, showing how exercise can dramatically change outcomes for cancer patients. With real-life stories from her work as a physiotherapist, she shares how movement can minimise treatment side effects, support recovery and improve outcomes for cancer patients. Kylie Moffitt is a multi-award-winning businesswoman, Physiotherapist,
Accredited Exercise Physiologist and Lymphoedema Therapist with over 25 years’ experience in health and medical care. She is the founder of PhysioHealth & Sports Injury Clinic and the driving force behind the CanConquer cancer rehabilitation program, both built on her core values of science, love, trust and pixie dust. Kylie’s mission is to reframe exercise as medicine and embed prehabilitation into standard cancer care, supporting people from the moment of diagnosis to strengthen their body for treatment and improve outcomes, rather than waiting for recovery. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference
title: Change your perspective: how exercise supports cancer treatment | Kylie Moffitt | TEDxWollongong

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sustainability claims are everywhere, but how much of it is real? Greenwashing expert John Pabon reveals three simple questions to ask that expose greenwashing, challenge us to think more critically about the claims we trust and better understand what genuine sustainability progress actually looks like. John Pabon has spent two decades in the business of saving our Earth. After leaving his role at the United Nations, John travelled the
world studying the impacts of sustainability first-hand in factories, on fields, and in Fortune 500s. He is widely considered Australia’s leading independent greenwashing expert. He is the author of “Sustainability for the Rest of Us: Your No-Bullshit, Five-Point Plan for Saving the Planet” and “The Great Greenwashing: How Brands, Governments, and Influencers are Lying to You.” This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What a Steel City Can Teach the World About Pragmatic Altruism  | John Pabon | TEDxWollongong

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Love can be weaponised. Kylee Dennis went from undercover cop to full-time fraud investigator after discovering her mother had been targeted by a romance scam, exposing the organised crime networks that exploit trust and manipulate longing for profit. Kylee Dennis is a former NSW Police detective turned scam investigator and educator. After nearly 14 years in law enforcement serving as an undercover operative, negotiator, and detective, Kylee
shifted her focus to combating one of today’s most insidious crimes: online romance scams. Driven by compassion and justice, she went undercover as both a 67-year-old man and a 62-year-old woman to expose how digital predators manipulate trust and emotion to exploit victims. Her work breaks the stigma surrounding victims of online deception and empowers people to protect themselves and others in the digital world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at ht
title: Your Next Great Love Story Could Be a Crime Scene | Kylee Dennis | TEDxWollongong

author: TEDx Talks
description: Think you understand sun protection? Think again. Nuwangi Cooray dismantles common assumptions about UV exposure and reveals why SPF numbers don’t tell the full story. Her work points toward a future where sunscreen is smarter, safer and designed for the realities of life under the harsh Australian sun. Nuwangi Pramuditha Cooray is the founder of Sun&Co, focusing on developing next generation, safer sunscreens designed specifically for Australia’s extreme ultraviolet (UV) environment. Her work stands at the intersection of nanotechnology, sustainability, and public health. By combining advanced nanomaterials with a new UV Index based testing method, she aims to bridge the gap between laboratory performance and real world protection, helping Australia lead global innovation in sun safety. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Lookout! The Future of Sunscreen Begins Under the Australian Sun | Nuwangi Cooray | TEDxWollongong

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most people treat disruption as a test—push harder, stay the course, rely on grit.

That instinct can cost years.

Chad Hyams shows how to recognize when a disruption calls for endurance and when it’s signaling a new direction. Chad Hyams is a leadership coach, speaker, and bestselling author who helps individuals and organizations navigate moments of uncertainty with clarity and intention. His work focuses on what happens when plans fall apart — and how leaders make better decisions when the path forward is no longer clear.

Known for his practical, whole-person approach, Chad challenges the belief that grit is always the answer. Instead, he teaches leaders how to recognize disruption as information, not failure, and how to respond with awareness rather than reflex.

He is the author of the bestselling book Achieve Your Apex and works with high-performing professionals who want to maximize their impact without burning out or forcing paths that no longer fit.

For TEDxLakeWorthBeach,
title: Not Every Disruption Is a Test | Chad Hyams | TEDxLake Worth Beach

author: TEDx Talks
description: Do we really need music - or is it just a cultural luxury? In this thought-provoking talk, Xiaoxiao challenges that assumption, revealing how music is deeply woven into human development, emotional health, and collective wellbeing. What we often dismiss as optional may in fact be essential to how we grow, connect, and thrive. Xiaoxiao Hou is a classically trained concert musician and scholar whose work bridges performance, psychology, and wellbeing. She began piano at the age of three and guzheng at five, performing in concerts across China and the UK. Xiaoxiao holds a BA in Music Education (China), postgraduate degrees in Musicology (Durham) and Applied Psychology (Leeds), and a PhD in Music Psychology from the University of Liverpool, where her research examined how music supports people living with dementia, integrating psychology, public health, and performance. She performs widely across the UK as a soloist and cultural ambassador, showcasing traditional Chinese instruments along
title: Why We Don’t Need Music (And Why We’re Wrong) | Xiaoxiao Hou, PHD, AFHEA | TEDxLCCM

author: TEDx Talks
description: Being a music artist today means navigating far more than creativity - it’s about surviving and adapting within powerful digital platforms. This talk unpacks how algorithms, branding, and constant visibility reshape what it means to make and share music. Beyond the art, artists must now master the system that determines whether their voices are heard. Annatoria (born Blessing Annatoria Chitapa) is a Zimbabwe-born British singer-songwriter and gospel/pop artist with over 2 million combined followers on Instagram and TikTok thanks to her powerful voice, engaging content, and inspiring presence online. Whilst studying music at LCCM, she rose to fame by winning The Voice UK in 2020 as the youngest winner in the show’s history, earning national recognition and a record deal. Since then, she’s released acclaimed music blending gospel, R&B, Afrobeats, and pop, including her EP Full Circle and seasonal project Present Jesu. Annatoria’s impact has been recognised with multiple awards, includin
title: Surviving the Platform | Blessing Annatoria Chitapa | TEDxLCCM

author: TEDx Talks
description: Music isn’t just art - it’s a living framework that shapes how we connect, belong, and remember. In this talk, we explore how sound acts as social architecture, building identity and preserving cultural memory across generations. Through rhythm and melody, communities don’t just express themselves - they construct shared meaning and lasting bonds. 'Christopher Barnett is a British film and television composer of Jamaican heritage, known for blending lush orchestral writing with contemporary electronic sound design. His work spans character-driven fiction and non-fiction feature films, including Speer Goes to Hollywood (IDA Best Score nominee), Tristram Shandy: A Cock and Bull Story (BAFTA-nominated), Borrowed Time (EIFF Best of the Fest), Getting Away With Murder(s), and All The Wild Horses, for which he won Best Music. Drawing on a background in jazz, 20th-century classical, chart music, and ethnomusicology, he records with orchestras in London, Budapest, and Bulgaria, and is represe
title: Music as Social Architecture  | Christopher Barnett | TEDxLCCM

author: TEDx Talks
description: Behind every pair of shoes lies a story of craftsmanship, patience and purpose. Without a traditional academic path, Dean Westmoreland built his journey through dedication to craft, showing how skill, discipline and passion can shape not just what we create, but who we become. Dean Westmoreland’s journey into footwear began unexpectedly at the age of 22, when he replied to a local newspaper advert for “shop duties including making tea.” That role turned out to be with Timpson, marking the start of a lifelong career in footwear. Working across a range of independent businesses, Dean developed an early ambition to create bespoke shoes. Living in Yorkshire, access to traditional shoemaking knowledge was limited, so he took a self-directed path, setting up his own shoe repair business with a specialist focus on welted footwear, while self-funding his shoemaking education. His continued passion for learning and mastery of leathercraft led to him being cast as a footwear expert on BBC One’s
title: More Than Shoes: A Story of Skill, Patience and Purpose | Dean Westmoreland | TEDxNorthampton

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it take to rediscover your passion for sport after life gets in the way? In his talk, Mr. Paul shares his personal journey as a cyclist and triathlete—from the pure joy of wind in his hair to the intense competition of the world stage.
He looks back to his early days, making provincial teams, and the devastating motorbike accident that shattered his dreams of competing in the 2000 Sydney Olympics. After years of focusing on family and career, a skiing accident four years ago became the unexpected catalyst for his "comeback".
And, his journey is far from over: after placing 2nd in his age group recently in a stacked competition, he's officially training for the 2026 World Championships in Japan. A primary school principal with a passion in sports, especially cycling. Just before the olympics, a motorcycle accident took him out of sports. Now, another accident brought him back into sports at a professional level. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference for
title: A Cycling Journey From Olympic Heartbreak to the World Stage | Gavin Paul | TEDxKaiwen Academy Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most people try to plan the perfect life—only to realize the best moments never made it onto the calendar. In this talk, Chris Abazis challenges our obsession with control and shows how spontaneity is the missing ingredient to a life that actually feels alive. What if the life you want isn’t something you plan… but something you allow? Chris Abazis is an entrepreneur, business coach, and professional instigator of forward motion. He helps founders, leaders, and creatives stop waiting for perfect conditions and start taking meaningful action—messy, human, and real.

Known for blending strategic thinking with humor and storytelling, Chris works at the intersection of decision-making, momentum, and authenticity. His approach challenges the idea that clarity comes before action, arguing instead that clarity is built by showing up, experimenting, and adjusting in real time.

Chris is the author of *Spontaneous AF*, a forthcoming book about intentional risk, presence, and choosing progress
title: Your Best Life Won’t Be on Your Calendar | Chris Abazis | TEDxLake Worth Beach

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk shifts the focus of sport away from visible moments of achievement to the systems that make them possible. It explores the discipline, consistency, and unseen effort that underpin performance, while questioning the way success is often defined and understood in competitive spaces. Manuel D'Souza is a distinguished figure in Indian sports, currently serving as the Head Strength and Conditioning (S&C) Coach for the Indian Men's Senior National Football Team. His journey represents a rare and successful transition from professional athletics to elite sports science, making him one of the most influential "backroom" figures in the modern era of the Blue Tigers. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What We Don’t See on Game Day | Manuel D'Souza | TEDxEMWS

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world where art is often perceived as effortless expression, this talk challenges that notion by uncovering the discipline that shapes it. Drawing from years of training in Kathak and an exploration of movement as both art and science, it examines how creativity is built through structure, repetition, and inquiry. It invites the audience to reconsider expression not as something spontaneous, but as something deeply constructed. At just 15 years old, Myra Barot, a student at Ecole Mondiale World School, has established herself as a formidable talent in the realm of Indian classical dance and has been recognized nationally. For over nine years, Myra has dedicated herself to the rigorous discipline of Kathak, and also published a research paper on the same. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Magic of Movement: Bridging the Mind and Body | Myra Barot | TEDxEMWS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk challenges the common belief that studying abroad is only for the wealthy.

Through real stories like Akshay, who pursued an MBA in Ireland with a limited budget, and Maaz, who studied in Hungary and went on to play for the national cricket team, the talk highlights how students from ordinary backgrounds can achieve global success.

It explains how scholarships, affordable destinations, part-time work opportunities, and the right guidance make international education more accessible than ever.

Blending these journeys with his own story, Asslam Shaikh emphasizes that the real barrier is not money, but mindset — and that with the right guidance, students can overcome financial limitations and build a future beyond borders. Asslam Shaikh is the Founder and CEO of Aliff, an edtech-driven study abroad consulting company having 85+ centers across India, Kuwait & Ghana. With over 15 years of experience, he has guided more than 32,000 students to pursue education across 19 countrie
title: You Don’t Need to Be Rich to Study Abroad | Asslam I Shaikh | TEDxBIT Jaipur

author: TEDx Talks
description: Everyday, countless people go through life with traumas unseen, unheard, unnoticed. In his speech, Mohamad shines a light on that “silent struggle”. Through research and personal insight, he argues that recognising pain, offering support, and breaking silence can save lives. In my speech, I talk about exposing the "Silent Struggle" pain that that plagues us today. Through studies and personal experiences, I reveal the true way to deal with people in need of support and to recognise that breaking the heavy silence can save a life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Echoes of The Unspoken | Mohamad Wehbe | TEDxWinchesterSchoolJebelAli

author: TEDx Talks
description: Public education changed the trajectory of my life.  As a migrant student growing up in poverty, raised by parents who lacked legal status, school was more than academics, it was stability, safety, and possibility. I did not succeed because the system was perfect, but because public education made room for me to learn before I fully understood the odds.  This talk reflects on how public education has historically served as a gateway to opportunity for students navigating fear, instability, and uncertainty and how, in today’s complex and political landscape, that promise requires intentional care.  Rather than focusing on policy, this talk centers on practice: the everyday decisions educators make that either widen or narrow opportunity. I share moments from my own schooling where small acts like being known by name, being protected from adult burdens, being encouraged without being singled out made a lasting difference. The talk offers three educator-centered strategies that help publ
title: What Public Education Gave Me — and How We Keep the Promise | Norma Castillo | TEDxBrewster Park ED
